content.value_statement: Accessibility gaps can block users and create compliance risk. This skill guides WCAG audits, barrier analysis, remediation planning, and retesting evidence.
actual_capabilities: Defines WCAG audit scope across pages, journeys, and conformance levels.
Guides automated testing with axe-core, jest-axe, pa11y, Puppeteer, and CI examples.
Provides manual checks for keyboard navigation, screen reader behavior, color contrast, and reflow.
Maps findings to severity, user impact, WCAG criteria, and remediation steps.
Outlines report sections for scores, violations, test results, fixes, and code examples.
limitations: Requires access to the product, page source, designs, or test environment.
Does not replace legal advice or formal certification from an accredited auditor.
Automated scans cannot prove complete WCAG conformance without manual testing.
Code samples need adaptation before production use.

use_cases.title: Pre-release WCAG audit
use_cases.description: Run checks on critical journeys and convert findings into reproducible tickets.

use_cases.title: Remediation backlog planning
use_cases.description: Prioritize accessibility barriers by user impact, severity, ownership, and release timing.

use_cases.title: Design system review
use_cases.description: Assess components for labels, focus states, contrast, keyboard behavior, and ARIA patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a page
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this page for WCAG 2.2 AA issues. Check keyboard use, headings, labels, contrast, focus order, and screen reader impact. Return prioritized fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Review a component
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this component for accessibility barriers. Assess states, labels, ARIA, keyboard behavior, focus handling, and error messages. Suggest exact remediation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Create a test plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an accessibility test plan for our release. Include automated scans, manual checks, assistive technology coverage, evidence capture, owners, and retest criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Build evidence package
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a WCAG compliance evidence package. Map each finding to success criteria, user impact, severity, fix owner, validation method, and retest result.

output_examples.input: Audit the checkout flow for WCAG 2.2 AA.
output_examples.output: A prioritized report identifies missing form labels, weak focus indicators, contrast failures, and retest steps for each issue.

output_examples.input: Review a modal dialog for accessibility.
output_examples.output: The review covers focus trapping, Escape key behavior, role usage, accessible names, and screen reader announcements.

output_examples.input: Plan accessibility checks for a release pipeline.
output_examples.output: The plan combines axe, pa11y, manual keyboard checks, evidence capture, ownership, and pass criteria.

best_practices: Define WCAG level, pages, user journeys, and assistive technologies before testing.
Combine automated scans with keyboard, screen reader, contrast, zoom, and reflow checks.
Retest every fixed issue and keep evidence linked to each WCAG criterion.
anti_patterns: Relying only on automated scanners for compliance decisions.
Treating color contrast fixes as the whole accessibility program.
Publishing audit reports without severity, user impact, ownership, and retest status.

faq.question: What WCAG versions does it support?
faq.answer: The guidance references WCAG 2.1 and WCAG 2.2 practices, with a focus on A and AA checks.

faq.question: Can it certify legal compliance?
faq.answer: No. It helps prepare evidence and remediation plans, but it does not replace legal review or formal certification.

faq.question: Does it require running tools?
faq.answer: Automated tools are recommended for baseline coverage, but manual review remains required for reliable results.

faq.question: Can it review designs before code exists?
faq.answer: Yes. It can inspect design artifacts for contrast, focus order, labels, error states, and inclusive interaction patterns.

faq.question: Does it work with screen readers?
faq.answer: It provides screen reader testing guidance and expected checks. Actual verification still needs a real assistive technology environment.

faq.question: Can teams use it in CI?
faq.answer: Yes. The playbook includes examples for axe, jest-axe, pa11y, and GitHub Actions workflows.
